claims.text: A CrMnFeCoNi-based system is an example of the refractory high-entropy alloy targeted by the hypothesis.
The initial alloy lacks a specialized heat-transfer microstructure.
The alloy is to be modified with approximately 2 atomic% tungsten.
The tungsten-doped alloy is to be annealed at about 1100°C for 15 minutes and then rapidly quenched.
The tungsten addition and rapid annealing will form coherent nanoscale tungsten-rich precipitates.
The tungsten-rich precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the HEA matrix.
Fine tungsten-rich precipitates will act as high-thermal-conductivity pathways.
Coherence between the precipitates and matrix will minimize lattice mismatch and stress concentrations.
Reduced lattice mismatch and stress concentration will preserve the alloy's mechanical strength.
Enhanced electronic and phonon conduction through the precipitates will increase overall thermal conductivity.
The modified alloy will retain improved performance at operating temperatures up to 800°C under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading representative of plasma exposure.
The intervention will measurably increase thermal conductivity relative to intermediate-layer HEAs processed without tungsten doping or post-synthesis annealing.
The intervention will maintain, or only negligibly affect, mechanical properties under expected reactor operating conditions.
Current intermediate-layer refractory HEAs processed without tungsten doping or high-temperature annealing lack the proposed enhanced heat-transfer pathways.
Prolonged exposure above 800°C may destabilize the precipitate microstructure.
Extreme irradiation may disrupt the coherent precipitate-matrix interfaces.

contradictions.description: The intervention comprises both tungsten doping and annealing, and the stated baseline lacks both treatments, but the experiment compares two tungsten-doped groups differing only in annealing. It therefore does not directly test the full intervention against the stated baseline or isolate the contribution of tungsten doping.
